transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because… I’ve been getting really bothered by how my face looks lately. Since we put in a brighter bathroom mirror, I keep noticing the skin around my cheeks and jaw, like it looks uneven or kind of saggy to me. My husband says he can’t really see what I’m talking about, but I keep seeing it.
How much time do you spend thinking about the way your face looks each day, and does it interfere with your usual activities or relationships?

I probably think about it on and off for maybe an hour or two a day, especially when I’m getting ready. I still get my work done, but I’ve spent extra time in the bathroom trying to look okay, and then I’ve had to rush into the courthouse a few mornings.

It’s also made me late to yoga more than once, like I miss the start because I was checking my face. And socially, I’ve skipped being in a few casual photos at book club or community events because I didn’t want to be worried about how my face would look.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like touching your face, adjusting your hair, or using makeup in a specific way, to try to fix or hide the way your face looks?

Yes. Most mornings I’ll check my face in the mirror from a few different angles before I leave, especially around my cheeks and jaw. Then I usually put on a little extra makeup to try to even it out or cover it.

And sometimes at work I catch myself comparing my face to other women’s faces. If I’m not feeling okay about how I look, I’ll avoid being in casual pictures too.
Has the way you feel about your face caused you any problems at work, with friends, or in other important areas of your life beyond what you’ve already mentioned?

Mostly it hasn’t stopped me from doing things, like I still get my work done. But it has caused some problems. I’ve spent too long getting ready and then had to rush into the courthouse a few mornings.

And outside of work, I’ve missed the start of yoga more than once because I was still checking my face. I’ve also skipped being in a few casual photos at book club and community events because I didn’t want to deal with worrying about how my face would look.
Do you feel that the way your face looks is so unattractive or abnormal that others would notice or judge you negatively because of it?

I guess… yes, to some extent. Since we put in that brighter bathroom mirror, I keep noticing the skin around my cheeks and jaw, like it looks uneven or a little saggy to me. My husband says he really can’t see what I’m talking about, but I still worry other people might notice it and think I look bad.
When you're worried about how your face looks, do you feel a strong urge to do something like checking the mirror repeatedly, adjusting your makeup, or seeking reassurance to reduce the distress?

Yes, I do. When I start worrying about it, I feel like I need to check the mirror again, usually from a couple different angles, and then I’ll add a little more makeup before I leave for the courthouse. It’s like I’m trying to feel sure it looks okay enough.

And sometimes later I catch myself comparing my face to women at work, or I’ll avoid being in casual pictures if I’m already feeling bad about it.
Do you find yourself avoiding situations or feeling very anxious in places where other people might be looking at you closely, like at public events, meetings, or even at work?

A little, yes. I don’t usually avoid work or meetings, but most mornings I do end up checking my face from a few angles and putting on a little extra makeup before I leave for the courthouse.

And if I’m already feeling bad about it, I might compare my face to women I see at work, or avoid being in casual pictures. It’s not constant, but it does happen.
Do you feel that the issue with your face is something that others would also see as a flaw, or do you think it’s something only you notice or would be bothered by?

I think… mostly it’s something I notice. I mean, to me the skin around my cheeks and jaw looks uneven, kind of saggy, especially in that brighter bathroom mirror. But my husband says he really can’t see what I’m talking about, so I don’t know if other people would actually see it the way I do.
Do you feel very upset or distressed when you think about how your face looks, like anxious or sad enough that it really affects your mood for the day?
I’m not sure I’d say it ruins my whole day. It can upset me in the moment, and I might feel anxious or down for a bit, especially if I’m getting ready. But usually I can still get on with things.
Do you feel that how your face looks is a very important part of how you see yourself or how others see you?

Yes, I think it has become more important to me than I’d like. I’m here because since we put in that brighter bathroom mirror, I keep noticing the skin around my cheeks and jaw looking uneven or kind of saggy. My husband says he can’t really see what I’m talking about, but I still keep focusing on it.
Do you find that your concern about how your face looks is something that comes up mostly on its own, or does it usually happen when you're already feeling down or anxious about other things?

It mostly comes up on its own, I think. Like, ever since we put in that brighter bathroom mirror, I just notice it when I’m looking at my face — the skin around my cheeks and jaw looks uneven or kind of saggy to me. It’s not always because I was already upset about something else. My husband says he can’t really see it, but I still keep focusing on it.
Do you feel that your concern about your face is something that takes up a lot of your time or causes you a lot of distress, even when you try not to focus on it?

Yeah, it does take up time, mostly when I’m in that bathroom mirror. I’ll notice the skin around my cheeks and jaw looking uneven or a little saggy, and then I keep checking it even though I’m trying not to. My husband says he doesn’t really see what I mean, but I still get stuck on it.
